messages.author: 6db3c86d422c5ae9
messages.subject: WRMR
parts:
Hello everyone,

I am testing the fit of my model. My questionnaire has three levels which are 0, 1 and 2. So that I used the estimator of wlsmv (DWLS) robust form. CFI and TLI are acceptable (.92 and .92, respectively). RMSEA is .04 which is good but WRMR is 1.61. Unfortunately, I do not know much about the WRMR. More specifically, I don't know about the value that is acceptable for WRMR. Does anyone know what value that is acceptable for WRMR? Should it be less than .1?

Thank you very much in advance,
Best regards,
Torres

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: WRMR
parts:
WRMR is developed by the Mplus team. They describe it as an
'experimental fit index'. In an unpublished technical report by Yu &
Muthen (2001), they suggest WRMR < 0.90 indicate good models (this is
mentioned in the technical appendices of Mplus).

See also http://www.statmodel.com/download/Yudissertation.pdf

where a cutoff of WRMR <= 1.0 is suggested.

Yves.
